Q115590816.summary: This Carolingian ivory casket, with its high gabled lid, is carved on every face with the story of Christ's infancy. On the side shown, the lid presents the Magi, in their Phrygian caps, bringing gifts to the Child, while the panel below shows Herod enthroned among armed guards as he receives the travellers from the East, all set within dense acanthus scrolls. Read around the box, the scenes unfold the mystery of the Incarnation from the Annunciation and Visitation to the Flight into Egypt.
facts: The Louvre attributes the casket to the 'second school of Metz' and dates it to about 870–880 on stylistic grounds.

Besides the Magi before Herod and the Adoration, the Louvre identifies the Dream of Joseph, the Visitation, the angel warning the sleeping Magi, an Annunciation (?), the Flight into Egypt, the Nativity and the Presentation in the Temple on the other faces.
Fixing holes show that a metal mount once covered the edges of the panels; the casket came from the collection of the Lyon painter Pierre Révoil and was bought by the Louvre in 1828.
Q115590816.notes: Inventory MRR 75. Date was given as '870s'; the Louvre gives c. 870–880 and Metz as place of making.
Q115590816.original_title: Coffret : Scènes de l'Enfance du Christ
